chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, who said:
I was in Fayd, so I walked with Ali ibn Bilal to the grave of Muhammad ibn Ismail ibn Bazi'. So Ali ibn Bilal said to me, 'The inhabitant of this grave narrated from Al-Rida (peace be upon him):'

'He said: Whoever comes to the grave of his brother, then places his hand upon the grave and recites 'Inna anzalnahu fi laylati al-qadr' seven times, will be secure from the Great Panic, or the Day of Panic.'

key_terms.الرِّضَا: Al-Rida (a title for Imam Ali ibn Musa, peace be upon him)
key_terms.الْفَزَعِ الْأَكْبَرِ: The Great Panic (a term for the Day of Judgment)
key_terms.صَاحِبُ الْقَبْرِ: The inhabitant of the grave (often referring to the deceased or a spiritual entity associated with it)

ai.seo_question: What is the benefit of reciting Surah Al-Qadr at a grave?
ai.summary: Recorded in Al-Kafi, this hadith links the ritual of visiting a grave with the specific act of touching it and reciting Surah Al-Qadr seven times, a practice attributed to Imam al-Rida (AS) via the deceased. It emphasizes the spiritual benefit of securing safety from the 'Great Panic' (Yawm al-Faza' al-Akbar), a key eschatological event in Shia tradition, thereby connecting intercessory visitation with divine mercy on Judgment Day.
